text: Harness: decomposition stage that proposes children with hypothesis, weight and cost until leaves fit one cycle
description: For a non-leaf or too-large open idea, the planner model returns 2-7 children: text, description with acceptance evidence, hypothesis (claim that could fail), weight, cost estimate, and 'executable in one cycle?' flag. Harness dedupes each against semantic search (reuse/link existing instead of creating), then creates them. Limits: max depth per cycle, max new ideas per cycle, stop decomposing when a child is executable. Children of high-value ideas can land as ai-proposition instead of open (see the human-gated decomposition proposition). Evaluate on existing graph: for implemented parents, compare proposed children with the real ones.

supportingConnections.hypothesis: Gating only strategy-level decompositions keeps the human as final authority on direction without making them review every small step.

Asking one well-chosen question before decomposing an ambiguous parent yields children closer to the human's intent than guessing; testable on the decomposition eval by masking parts of parent descriptions.

status.comment:
Decompose stage done: up to config.decomposition.maxChildren (default 7) children with description/acceptance, hypothesis, weight, cost; links an existing similar idea instead of creating; one decompose per cycle (depth 1, new ideas <= maxChildren, enforced in cycle.ts); harness.json decomposition.landingState can land all children as ai-proposition. The value-threshold variant lives in its child 5e431a84 (ai-proposition, waits on Felix).

Evaluation against real children (scripts/eval-decomposition.ts, resumed 2026-11-09, planner nvidia/z-ai/glm-5.3-flash, harness defaults, no tools so hidden children cannot leak): 8 implemented parents with 3-7 implemented children each, every parent got a submission (noSubmission 0). Mean best cosine of each real child to the nearest proposal 0.687 vs 0.555 for the shuffled control (proposals scored against another parent's children): the planner finds the right area clearly above chance. Near-restatements are rare: coverage at cosine >= 0.8 is 5% (control 0%), 0 at 0.85/0.9. Reading: the planner proposes a plausible but different split than the human did, not the same children; with n=8 and bge cosine a weak separator (most high pairs are intended splits), treat this as a baseline for comparing models or prompts, not a quality verdict. Results: .bowman/runtime/evals/decomposition-glm53.json (+ .proposals.jsonl).
